chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from an-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Ibn Sinan said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who is making up for Ramadan, becomes junub from the beginning of the night, and does not perform ghusl until the end of the night, while he believes that dawn has risen. He (AS) said: 'He does not fast that day, and he fasts another day.'

Al-Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And whoever becomes a fasting person for making up a day from the month of Ramadan, and breaks his fast in it unintentionally (out of forgetfulness), there is no blame is not upon him, and he completes the rest of his day with fasting.

key_terms.قَضَاءِ رَمَضَانَ: Making up missed days of Ramadan

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one delays ghusl until after dawn while making up Ramadan fasts?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between intentional neglect and forgetfulness in the context of *Qada* (making up) Ramadan fasts. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that if one delays *ghusl* until after dawn with the belief that dawn has broken, the fast is invalidated, requiring a makeup day; however, if the break is due to forgetfulness, the fast remains valid and is completed for the remainder of the day. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that *junub* status does not inherently break the fast unless accompanied by eating, drinking, or intentional acts after dawn, highlighting the mercy in easing obligations for those who are unaware or forgetful.
